items.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: I heard Tommy Dorsey’s [scats] and he’d play that long trombone solo on it, which was very nice.

ctx.x: Was there ever a conflict between your choice of jazz oriented music and your spirituality? Was there any kind of — these don’t work together for you? © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Well as a kid I’d heard that the blues and rhythm was the devil’s music. And I didn’t really listen to the blues that much. I heard it, because it was a part of the scene. Getting back to that high school thing, I remember hearing Louis Jordan swing on the jukebox, singing “Caldonia” and all those things, and I’d see them in movies and I heard Tommy Dorsey’s [scats] and he’d play that long trombone solo on it, which was very nice.
